thought.text: There are many releases. Let me verify the binary integrity (sha256) and test whether an older version runs, to isolate whether this is a bad download or an environment incompatibility:

reasoning_content:
There are many releases available. The one I downloaded (2025-09-07) is segfaulting. Let me test a few other versions to see if this is version-specific or a general environmental issue (e.g., Go runtime incompatibility). Let me try several in parallel. Actually, let me first test 2024-12-13 (an older one) and 2025-04-22 to check whether older builds work.

Actually, wait a sec. Let me think about this segfault. The mc client (Go 1.24.6) runs without any problem. The minio server segfaults on --version. Both are Go binaries. This is suspicious. If mc works, then Go itself works. So why does minio segfault?

Possibility: minio might be built with a specific Go version that uses a feature not supported in this environment, or minio might use CGO with a specific library. Or maybe the downloaded binary is corrupted.

Let me check the sha256 of the binary I downloaded and compare it with the .sha256sum provided by GitHub. If it matches, then the binary is fine and it's an environmental issue.

Let me try a few things:
1. Verify the sha256
2. Try a different (older) minio version

Let me do this efficiently.

action.command:
cd /tmp
TAG="RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z"
echo "=== verify sha256 of downloaded server ==="
curl -sSL -m 30 "https://github.com/minio/minio/releases/download/${TAG}/minio.linux-amd64.${TAG}.sha256sum" | awk '{print "expected: "$1}'
sha256sum minio_server | awk '{print "actual:   "$1}'
echo "=== test older version 2024-12-13 ==="
OLD="RELEASE.2024-12-13T22-19-12Z"
timeout 120 curl -sSL -o minio_old "https://github.com/minio/minio/releases/download/${OLD}/minio.linux-amd64.${OLD}" -w "HTTP %{http_code} size=%{size_download}\n"
chmod +x minio_old
timeout 10 ./minio_old --version 2>&1 | head -3; echo "old exit=$?"
